summary.one_liner: A Markdown quick-reference cheat sheet of common Git commands plus a Git Flow (git-flow-avh) section, available in several translations.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a categorized reference of Git commands with short bash snippets and brief notes. Sections cover setup and configuration files (system, global, local scopes), creating or cloning repositories, staging and committing, amending, stashing, and searching with git grep and git log -S. It also covers history inspection, branches and tags, remotes, fetch/pull/push, merge and rebase with conflict resolution, and several ways to undo changes (reset, revert, checkout). A separate Git Flow section lists git-flow-avh install commands and feature, release, and hotfix workflows. Warnings appear around amending or rebasing published commits and force-deleting branches. Links to translated versions in about eleven languages are included.
use_cases: look up a Git command without memorizing it
undo or revert commits and discard local changes
clean up or squash commits before publishing
set up Git identity and configuration
follow a git-flow branching model for features, releases, and hotfixes
find which commit introduced a keyword
notable: Covers both plain Git commands and the git-flow-avh branching workflow in one page
Available in about eleven translated versions, including Arabic, Chinese, German, and Spanish
Includes warnings about amending or rebasing published commits
Shows the config scope table (repository, user, system) with matching flags
caveats: Many commands are templates with placeholder arguments that were stripped from the README, so some examples are incomplete
Git Flow install instructions for Windows rely on Cygwin with wget and util-linux
Some commands are presented without explanation of their effects
